entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Antonio Malfante (\?–1450) was a Genoese trader known for traveling to Africa on behalf of the Centurione Bank in 1447.

He played a crucial role in the exchange of goods between Europe and Africa during the 15th century.

Malfante's voyages contributed to the growth of trade networks and the spread of cultural and economic influences across the Mediterranean region.

His legacy can be seen in the development of maritime trade routes and the establishment of new trade relationships between European and African societies.
